title: Majenius Move
reviewNotes: Two branches, seven exact positions from the complete seven-piece phase after ...hxg6 at 78s. Earlier nine-/ten-piece sacrifices remain source context. Kxf6 forces ...g5; Kf5 forces ...g4 and hxg4 mate. Independent Ke5 loses by releasing the king.
transcript: Sometimes it's not enough to be a genius once per game. You have to be [music] a genius multiple times to be able to win. In this position, black is left with an entire queen and a bunch of pawns, [music] whereas white is only left with a bishop and a knight. So, it might seem like black is completely winning, but white has an incredible hidden resource. And the plan starts with a king to F5. Now, making sure that the black king is stuck on the edge of the [music] board. And we start to realize that black doesn't actually have many moves available. All of the pawns and the king are stuck. So, it has to move the queen. But, taking the knight would simply result in a checkmate in one move. Moving here would allow a fork of the queen and king. And moving here would simply hang the queen. So, black is left with only one option, the F8 square. But, this should not be a problem, right? The queen is simply going to be able to escape, and then black is going to be completely [music] winning. But, white starts to show his cards and plays the first brilliant move in this position. Knight to G7, sacrificing the knight completely. And of course, the knight has to be taken because this is almost a checkmate. And after the queen takes, we can now follow up with bishop to E8. At first glance, it seems like black is doomed. But, then we realize that black can actually sacrifice the queen like this, [music] with a check, where it is forced to take. And after it does, black is going to capture back. And now, there is no checkmate. Black is left with four pawns against one, and it's still going to win. But, [music] actually the game is already over because white captures this pawn, and there is only one move available for black, to push the G pawn. And now, after king to F5, black is in zugzwang. The best move would be to not move anything whatsoever. And white would have no way to make any progress. But, black, according [music] to the rules of chess, has to move the only piece that can move in this position, the pawn, and allow H takes G4. Checkmate. If you love incredible chess, follow for more.
